summary.name: The Checklist Manifesto
summary.one_liner: A 2009 book by surgeon Atul Gawande arguing that well-designed checklists help experts in complex fields like medicine, aviation and construction avoid mistakes.
use_cases: Reading about how checklists reduce errors in complex work
Designing checklists for surgical or clinical teams
Understanding how pilots and builders use checklists
Learning about global surgical safety programs
Finding reading material for reliability and site reliability engineering
summary.what_it_does: The page is a landing page for Atul Gawande's book The Checklist Manifesto, containing excerpted reviews rather than product features. Malcolm Gladwell's review describes the book's argument: errors of ignorance versus errors of ineptitude, with failure in modern life mostly coming from failing to use existing knowledge properly. Gawande examines pilots and skyscraper builders and proposes checklists as a remedy. The final section describes his team developing a safe surgery checklist and applying it internationally. Steven Levitt's Freakonomics review says the book shows that even expert teams benefit from well-designed checklists, and mentions stories about pilots, Walmart's response to Hurricane Katrina, and a rock band's backstage M&M's rider. The page also lists the book's bestseller status on several major lists.
notable: Covers errors of ignorance versus errors of ineptitude in complex work
Includes stories from aviation, skyscraper construction and medicine
Describes the development and international rollout of a safe surgery checklist
Author is a surgeon and Harvard public health researcher
caveats: Page contains only reviews and author bio; no purchase, price or edition details
Reviews are excerpts from third parties, not a full description of the book
